documentation.summary: Grid arithmetic: auto, f32 or f64
documentation.details: auto grids in f64 on the CPU, as CASA does, and in f32 on Metal; f32 halves the memory of every grid, at the cost of a running sum that drifts with the number of samples each grid cell takes. Metal accumulates in f32 only, so f64 keeps backend = auto on the CPU and is refused with backend = gpu.

documentation.summary: Log one timing event per imaging phase
documentation.details: Each phase (preparation, setup, every major and minor cycle, products) logs at INFO, under target casa_imaging::stage_timing, its wall time, the process's peak resident memory and the memory admission held: the phase record of <imagename>.summary.json. The events reach stderr when its priority admits INFO (--log-stderr-priority INFO), and the log table at its own priority. They change nothing the run computes.

documentation.summary: Log the Metal backend's timing for each gridding owner, prediction batch and wave
documentation.details: When the run grids on Metal (backend = gpu, or auto on the GPU), each Metal backend that dispatched logs at INFO, under target casa_imaging::metal_stage_timing, when its wave of a pass ends: each gridding owner, and each row chunk's backend that predicts the model of a native-channel residual. It logs whether its work completed, its dispatches, samples (of which predicted) and sub-blocks (counted as requested, so a failed backend's include work never done), the kernel cells it uploaded, the host's preparation time and its waits for the device, and the device's time on its commands (summed per command, so concurrent backends' sums can exceed the wall time, and the span from the first command's start to the last one's end). Each wave also logs its source stream: the blocks, the producer's time filling them and how long the pass waited for a filled block. A CPU run logs nothing.

documentation.summary: Log the clean controller's science quantities at each cycle
documentation.details: Logs at INFO, under target casa_imaging::science_trace, the residual statistics each cleaning decision reads (peak in and outside the mask, PSF sidelobe, n-sigma threshold, mask size), each minor cycle's controls (iteration limit, cycle threshold, gain), and what each minor cycle cleaned. They change nothing the run computes.

Device the major-cycle passes grid on: auto, cpu or gpu
documentation.details: auto grids on the GPU where it runs the request and on the CPU otherwise; the run summary records which. gpu is Metal on macOS, needs a unified-memory Metal 3 device, grids in f32 and runs the standard gridder (W projection, mosaic and AW projection run on the CPU); a request it cannot run is refused. Choosing the GPU accepts f32 grids, so an explicit gridprecision = f64 keeps auto on the CPU. auto also keeps on the CPU what no GPU-against-CPU law covers yet: outlier fields, polarizations other than Stokes I, and runs that write MODEL_DATA or CORRECTED_DATA. Sample placement stays on the CPU workers; on the GPU, the model is also predicted at native channels and the residual formed there.

documentation.summary: AW convolution-function cell cache size in MiB, or auto
documentation.details: An integer bounds the AW catalog's shared cell cache to that many MiB, as before. auto sizes it once the run has chosen its workers: it starts at 256 MiB and grows into the memory the worker fit leaves free, up to every cell of the catalog, so it never costs a worker. A cache that holds every cell reads each one once; a smaller one evicts and rereads cells every pass.
